items.title: Fannie Mae slashes 2027 mortgage forecast amid higher rates
items.description: Fannie Mae ’s Economic and Strategic Research Group cut its 2027 mortgage origination forecast by 18% in its October outlook, signaling that mortgage rates are expected to stay higher and refinance volume will remain weak. The ESR Group now projects total single-family originations in 2027 will reach $1.86 trillion, down from $2.27 trillion in its September forecast. For this year, Fannie Mae economists still expect about $2 trillion in volume. Higher rate assumptions are driving the downgrade, with the Federal Reserve (Fed) expected to continue raising interest rates — the next Federal Open Market Committe e meeting concludes Oct. 28. Fannie Mae now expects 30-year mortgage rates to average 7.5% in 2026, up from 6.7% in the September outlook. Refinance activity takes the brunt of the revision. Fannie Mae now expects 2027 refinance originations of about $430 billion, roughly half of the prior $802 billion estimate and below the approximately $695 billion projected for this year. Purchase originations are forecast to total $1.4 trillion in 2027, essentially flat with this year, underscoring that the market will remain purchase-driven. On the macroeconomic front, the ESR Group kept its outlook for real gross domestic product growth at a 2.5% increase, suggesting the weaker mortgage outlook is more about rates than recession risk. Inflation expectations edged higher, with the Consumer Price Index now projected to rise 1.9% year over year in the fourth quarter of 2027, compared with 1.7% in the prior forecast. Feeling the strain “Rates have gotten higher than what anybody expected, compared to where people were expecting things to be six months ago,” said Gagan Sharma, founder and CEO at BSI Financial . “What is that manifesting itself? Servicing is more expensive than it ever has been, origination has been harder but the economy is doing great actually.” Fannie Mae’s view differs somewhat from that of the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), which also assumes elevated rates and subdued volume but with its own trajectory. The MBA’s baseline forecast released during their annual convention this week in Chicago calls for 30-year mortgage rates to remain above 7% through 2027, after reaching 7.5% last week. At those levels, MBA economists expect total single-family mortgage originations to decline 5% to $1.99 trillion in 2027, down from $2.1 trillion projected for 2026. For MBA economists, that backdrop points to more consolidation among independent mortgage banks. “At the height in 2021, we were at about 881 companies (independent mortgage banks), and that’s now down to 707 at the end of 2025 – so, that doesn’t even account for what’s happened this past year,” Marina Walsh, vice president and head of industry analysis at the MBA, said. She added, “There has been a movement toward consolidation. I do think that M A activity may continue, especially if companies feel like they have to make big investments, big technology investments and they’re not capable of doing that. But if they join forces with another company that has the capital, has the cash to do so, it would make a lot of sense.” Related More: Fannie Mae Mortgage Rates

items.title: First Horizon sells $4.5B mortgage portfolio at discount
items.description: Tennessee-based First Horizon Bank agreed to sell about $4.5 billion of residential mortgage loans at roughly a 10% discount in the third quarter as it moves to align its mortgage production more closely with core relationship clients, the bank told analysts Thursday. The portfolio carries a weighted average coupon of 3.85% and only about $200 million of associated deposits, according to the bank . First Horizon entered into a sale agreement in October and expects to settle the sale early in the fourth quarter. The buyer’s name was not disclosed. “This transaction further ensures our balance sheet is aligned with our strategic focus on delivering relationship oriented banking and focusing on safety and soundness, profitability and growth,” Hope Dmuchowski, senior executive vice president and chief financial officer, said on the bank’s earnings call. Chairman, president and CEO Bryan Jordan said during the call that the sale is happening now because it “became clear that we are in a cycle of rising rates.” “We size the portfolio based on trying to extract out or sell what were essentially nonrelationship portfolio assets,” Jordan said. “We looked at the portfolio, tried to exclude anything that was related to private clients or wealth.” The bank said it expects the deal to be accretive over time. Management projected a roughly 4% benefit to 2027 earnings per share and an improvement in return on tangible common equity of about 150 basis points. First Horizon also expects its loan-to-deposit ratio to move to approximately 88%, strengthening its liquidity position. To reflect the pending sale, First Horizon recorded a $473 million impact to other noninterest income tied to the mortgage portfolio. The bank reported a net loss of about $79 million for the quarter. Related More: Earnings MBS

items.title: Single-Family Permitting Declines Through August
items.description: Single-Family Permitting Declines Through August – Eye On Housing Skip to content Search Research/Data Housing Economics Plus Books Dashboards Local Data Research Studies Services Indices Team Videos Research/Data Housing Economics Plus Books Dashboards Local Data Research Studies Services Indices Team Videos Eye On Housing National Association of Home Builders Economic Research Blog Single-Family Permitting Declines Through August October 16, 2026 Danushka Nanayakkara-Skillington No Comments Single-family permitting activity continued to soften through the first eight months of 2026, while multifamily permitting remained stronger compared with the same period last year. Regional and state-level trends show continued variation in permitting activity, reflecting differences in housing demand, affordability conditions, and local market dynamics. Over the first eight months of the year, the number of single-family permits issued nationwide reached 620,558. Compared with the same period in 2025, this represents a 2.6% decline from the August 2025 total of 637,096. In contrast, multifamily permitting activity remained stronger, with 347,629 permits issued nationwide, marking a 5.1% increase compared with the same period last year. Regionally, year-to-date single-family permitting declined in three out of the four regions through August. The Midwest was the only region to post an increase, with single-family permits rising 2.0%. The South declined 2.0%, the West fell 5.2%, and the Northeast posted the largest decline, at 9.4%. Multifamily permits increased in three of the four regions, led by the Northeast (31.0%), followed by the West (14.3%), and the Midwest (2.7%). The South was the only region to post a decline, with multifamily permits falling 5.6%, driven largely by reduced permitting activity in major metropolitan areas across the region. At the state level, 23 states and the District of Columbia recorded increases in single-family permits compared with the same period last year, with gains ranging from 65.6% in the District of Columbia to 0.2% in Oklahoma. The remaining 27 states posted declines. Nevada recorded the steepest decline, with single-family permits falling 26.3%. The ten states issued the highest number of single-family permits accounted for 62.4% of all single-family permits issued nationwide. Texas led the nation with 98,378 permits issued through August 2026, although this represented a 3.4% decline from the same period in 2025. Florida, the second-highest state, recorded a 1.3% decline, while North Carolina, ranking third, posted a 7.5% decrease. Through August, 26 states and the District of Columbia recorded increases in multifamily building permits, while 24 states experienced declines. Alabama posted the largest percentage increase, with multifamily permits rising 76.3%, from 1,227 to 2,163 units. In contrast, Louisiana recorded the steepest decline, with permits falling 65.5%, from 2,400 to 829 units. The ten states issued the highest number of multifamily permits accounted for 60.9% of all multifamily permits issued nationwide. Through the first eight months of 2026, Texas, which issued the largest number of multifamily permits, posted a 17.2% decline compared with the same period last year. California, the second-highest state, recorded a 25.5% increase, while Florida, ranking third, saw multifamily permits decrease by 28.1%. items.title: Wu Secures Approval To Give Tax Breaks To 4 Big Multifamily Projects
items.description: Wu Secures Approval To Give Tax Breaks To 4 Big Multifamily Projects October 16, 2026 | 6:13 pm ET Jon Banister, East Coast Editor Large-scale development has ground to a halt in Boston, and the city government is now offering tens of millions in tax breaks to try to get a series of big projects moving. But it remains to be seen whether the money will be enough to move the needle. Boston Planning Department A rendering of Fulcrum Global Investors' One Mystic Ave. in Charlestown Mayor Michelle Wu 's proposal to offer property tax abatements for market-rate housing developments totaling more than 1,400 units secured approval Thursday evening from the Boston Planning Development Agency Board. The administration can now move forward on negotiations with developers over the abatements, which are estimated to total $31.5M in temporary tax relief. Four projects were approved for the abatements: A 424-unit building from Fulcrum Global Investors at 1 Mystic Ave. in Charlestown. A 341-unit building from New England Development at the Allston Yards complex. A 333-unit building from Nordblom Co . at 83 Leo M. Birmingham Parkway in Brighton. A 316-unit building from Hines at 22-24 Pratt St. in Allston. These projects, which Wu's administration proposed for the tax abatements last month , are serving as a pilot for the initiative, which it hopes to later expand. Another 10 to 12 developers have expressed interest, Reuben Kantor, a senior policy adviser for the Boston Planning Department, said at Thursday's meeting. City officials say they targeted larger buildings because they have been the hardest to get underway. According to a Planning Department presentation , three 100-plus-unit projects per year have broken ground over each of the last four years, and zero projects with more than 300 units have started construction. Officials say this is because developers can't make nearly the same return on investment on these buildings that they could in the past. And average returns are barely above the return an investor can get from the 10-year Treasury, which has risen above 5% , making it harder to raise equity for a project. Boston Planning Department A slide from a Planning Department presentation showing how housing starts have fallen along with the average return on investment for developments They attribute these shrinking returns to rising costs. While rents have risen 35% since 2015, that is outpaced by the 38% increase in construction costs and the 133% spike in mortgage interest payments, according to the presentation. To receive the tax abatement, developers must start construction within the next 12 to 15 months. Taxes would remain at their current rate throughout the construction period, and after a project reaches completion — the point when a property's value jumps — the rise in taxes would be spread over a series of years. The Wu administration said the city will ultimately experience no net revenue loss, as developers' tax payments would be delayed rather than forgiven. That structure may not be enough to change the equation for many projects, which are having a hard time securing the construction financing needed to start the process. Aeron Hodges, a principal at Stantec Architecture , said at a Bisnow event last month that she is working with three of the four development teams that are receiving this initial round of abatements. She asked them how much of a difference they would make, and the response was “pretty uncertain.” “It helps on the operations down the road, but the immediate [financing] needs for putting the project in ground is still fundamentally challenging,” she said. The Planning Department's Kantor acknowledged at the meeting that it is a “very modest tax relief offer” that won't work for every project, but he said he thinks it will allow these four to get off the ground. items.title: TruAmerica nabs 446 units to surpass 3K threshold in Atlanta metro area
items.description: An article from TruAmerica nabs 446 units to surpass 3K threshold in Atlanta metro area The firm relied on an existing relationship to help secure the Gables Residential-built Bricks at Perimeter Center from seller Clark Ventures. Published Oct. 16, 2026 Leslie Shaver Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Bricks at Perimeter Center in Dunwoody, Ga. Permission granted by TruAmerica Multifamily Property: Bricks at Perimeter Center Buyer: TruAmerica Multifamily Seller: Clark Ventures Property type: Garden-style Units: 446 Location: Dunwoody, Georgia In Sun Belt multifamily right now, it's a tale of two markets. At the lower end of the scale are assets built in the 1980s and 1990s that suffer from deferred maintenance and are caught in a liquidity crunch. On the other end of the spectrum are newer class A properties in neighborhoods with limited supply and strong employment drivers. That’s where the investment dollars are focused right now, according to Julien Lipps, director of acquisitions for the Southeast region at TruAmerica Multifamily. On Oct. 15, TruAmerica announced it acquired one of those properties in the second bucket: the 446-unit Bricks at Perimeter Center garden-style apartment community in Dunwoody, Georgia, which sits within Atlanta’s Perimeter Center submarket, according to a press release shared with Multifamily Dive. The firm acquired the Gables Residential-built property from Atlanta-based Clark Ventures, according to Lipps. “The majority of the capital that is investing in multifamily in this turbulent environment is really all congregating in the same type of asset profile, which is why you're seeing dozens and dozens of bids on assets like the Bricks,” Lipps told Multifamily Dive. “Then, on an older vintage deal in a B location, it's very hard to sell those deals right now all across the United States, regardless of location.” TruAmerica used existing relationships to secure the deal. Earlier this year, the firm bought a property in Atlanta's Buckhead area, according to Lipps. Bricks owner Jordan Clark was part of that ownership group and was with Gables when the asset was built, according to Lipps. While buying the Buckhead property, TruAmerica told Clark Ventures it was seeking other acquisitions for its discretionary fund. CBRE Vice Chairman Kevin Geiger facilitated the deal, which brings the firm to 3,374 units in Atlanta. “We used our extensive relationship with Clark Ventures, and we were able to do something preemptively before the actual marketing process finished,” Lipps said. “We were able to take it off the shelves that way. Up until that point, they had 40 to 50 tours. So they were expecting maybe 25 to 30 bids.” An upgrade opportunity Bricks at Perimeter Center, built in 2007, features studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments with an average-sized floor plan of approximately 926 square feet, per the release. “It's very unique from a physical construction perspective,” Lipps said. “On top of that, it's an elevator product. You have penthouse units that have 15- to 20-foot ceilings, depending on the building.” Bricks at Perimeter Center also has four courtyards — two of which contain lake-like water features, according to Lipps. “There's a ton of opportunity to elevate those amenities and create a living experience for residents that you can't get even at some new construction properties,” Lipps said. TruAmerica plans to renovate 442 of the 446 units, according to the release. In individual apartments, the firm will install quartz countertops, stainless-steel appliances, new flooring and updated cabinetry and hardware. The property's original leasing office is now an unused clubhouse, according to Lipps. items.title: Build-to-rent now eligible for Federal Housing Administration financing
items.description: An article from Dive Brief Build-to-rent now eligible for Federal Housing Administration financing Under the policy change, BTR projects can qualify for new construction and acquisition or refinancing programs, as HUD pushes to increase housing supply. Published Oct. 16, 2026 Julie Strupp Senior Editor Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Kent Nishimura via Getty Images Listen to the article 3 min This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . Dive Brief: Build-to-rent housing is now eligible for Federal Housing Administration-insured financing through two of its multifamily mortgage insurance programs, according to an announcement from HUD. The update is effective immediately. Multifamily rentals that consist of single-family homes, duplexes or triplexes, including site-built and manufactured, will now be treated under the same terms and conditions as traditional multifamily rental developments. The shift reflects the “expanding presence of professionally managed” build-to-rent communities and the growing demand for them, per the release. HUD’s update applies to FHA's Section 221(d)(4) program for new construction as well as its Section 223(f) program for acquisition or refinancing of recently developed rental communities, according to a mortgagee letter that outlines eligibility criteria . Dive Insight: Historically, the Office of Multifamily Housing limited its insured loans to developments with buildings containing four or more units, according to the letter. “BTR properties were excluded due to their single-family design and subdivision-style layout that raised concerns about Fair Housing Act compliance (particularly, accessibility design requirements) and valuation and underwriting challenges,” the letter reads. The FHA’s policy change aims to make it easier to finance new rentals and increase the overall housing supply, “particularly in light of manufactured housing innovation,” according to the release. Production of manufactured housing has dwindled from its peak in the 1970s and 1980s, with the drop in production due in part to HUD’s 1974 permanent chassis mandate that added up to $10,000 to the development cost of a new unit, Smart Cities Dive reported. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act , which became law in July, updated manufactured housing regulations and eliminated that chassis requirement. Now HUD plans to explore new manufactured housing designs that can be built quickly. To qualify for FHA funding, BTR properties must be developed on a single uninterrupted site and operated as a single property and in a similar fashion to other multifamily projects on the market, per the mortgagee letter. Projects consisting of a mix of multifamily housing, with a BTR component along with traditional apartment buildings, are permitted. Although manufactured or modular construction is allowed, the agency does note that these methods “add challenges to HUD’s traditional approach to insuring advances for work installed on-site, and these issues must be carefully vetted at the concept meeting,” according to the mortgagee letter. Expanding the overall rental housing supply is key to improving affordability, according to Joe Gormley, who oversees the FHA and Office of Housing. “Combined with other initiatives we are working on at HUD, including chassis removal in our manufactured housing programs, we are unshackling the market to deliver housing where it’s needed most,” Gormley said in the release. items.title_zh: Newmark警示$179B低息地产贷款面临refi风险
items.summary_zh: 78%地产债务再融资利率高于10-year Treasuries，高债务成本加剧违约压力

items.title: TMG, KKR Acquire San Jose's Skyport Plaza from Hudson Pacific
items.description: California CRE News In Your Inbox. Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. California + Bay Area + Office | October 16, 2026 By: Paul Bubny TMG, KKR Acquire San Jose’s Skyport Plaza from Hudson Pacific TMG Partners has acquired Skyport Plaza, a 435,000-square-foot office and retail complex located at 1650 Technology Dr., 1700 Technology Dr., 50 Skyport Dr. and 90 Skyport Dr. in San Jose. TMG Partners acquired the asset together with accounts managed by KKR. The seller was Hudson Pacific Properties, which announced a $75.5-million sale price. In conjunction with the acquisition, TMG signed a long-term, 393,000-square-foot lease with the County of Santa Clara. The 30-year lease is expected to commence in the first quarter of 2029, following extensive renovations to the two office buildings, formerly occupied by Qualcomm and now 100% vacant. The retail is fully occupied. “We’re pleased to support the County of Santa Clara in their consolidation at Skyport Plaza which will provide a more efficient and modern experience for their employees,” said TMG co-CEO Ben Kochalski. “We look forward to working with them on the property improvements to modernize the infrastructure for their staff, as well as provide a location where they can conveniently access services and restaurants.” Read More News Stories About: KKR Connect Inside The Story About Paul Bubny Paul Bubny serves as Senior Content Director for Connect Commercial Real Estate, a role to which he brings 19-plus years’ experience covering the commercial real estate industry and 35-plus years in business-to-business journalism. In this capacity, he oversees daily operations while also reporting on both local/regional markets and national trends, covering individual transactions across all property types, as well as delving into broader subject matter. He produces 11-15 daily news stories per day and works with the Connect team and clients to develop longer-form content, ranging from Q As to thought-leadership pieces. Prior to joining Connect, Paul was Managing Editor for both Real Estate Forum and GlobeSt.com at American Lawyer Media, where he oversaw operations at both publications while also producing daily news and feature-length articles. His tenure in B2B publishing stretches back into the print era, and he has served as Editor in Chief on four national trade publications. Since 1999, Paul has volunteered as the newsletter editor of passenger rail advocacy groups (one national, one local). items.title: Greenheck Group to Open 1.3 MSF Manufacturing Facility in Owasso, Oklahoma
items.description: OWASSO, OKLA. — Greenheck Group, a provider of commercial air movement, control and conditioning equipment, will open a 1.3 million-square-foot manufacturing facility in Owasso, a northern suburb of Tulsa. Greenheck has acquired a 72-acre distribution campus that was formerly operated by Macy’s, and the new manufacturing plant is expected to generate about 700 new jobs within the local economy over the next five years. items.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $216M Loan for Refinancing of Manhattan Office, Retail Building
items.description: NEW YORK CITY — Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $216 million bridge loan for the refinancing of 568 Broadway, a 390,745-square-foot office and retail building in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The 12-story building’s retail component totals 70,870 square feet retail and was fully leased at the time of the loan closing to tenants such as Hugo Boss, Athletic Propulsion Labs, GU and Equinox. Office users include Zocdoc, The Farmer’s Dog and Milk Makeup. items.title: Site Centers To Stop Trading As It Winds Up Operations
items.description: Site Centers plans to stop selling shares on the New York Stock Exchange after paying a $157M dividend to its investors.
items.selector_reason: Site Centers计划停止在纽交所交易，并向投资者支付1.57亿美元股息，显示该上市购物中心REIT正在结束公开市场运营。事件涉及REIT资本结构和资产退出，对机构投资者具有重要信号意义。
items.title_zh: Site Centers停牌并结束运营，先派发$157M股息
items.summary_zh: 公司将停止NYSE交易并清算运营，零售REIT投资退出信号偏负面

items.title: Mortgage bond sales put on hold as investors demand more yield
items.description: Figure Technology Solutions put a break on fundraising plans with a unit deciding to postpone a $346 million residential mortgage-backed security.
items.selector_reason: 一笔3.46亿美元住宅按揭证券化融资因投资者要求更高收益率而推迟，显示住房信贷资本市场出现定价压力。该事件对RMBS发行和非银行贷款机构融资具有中等以上行业影响。
items.title_zh: 投资者要求更高收益，$346M mortgage bond发行暂停
items.summary_zh: Figure推迟$346M RMBS募资，收益率要求上升显示住宅信用市场趋紧

items.title: Home equity deal shows VantageScore viable for RMBS ratings
items.description: A fintech's transaction is the first to go through S&P Global's preliminary rating process with VantageScore 4.0 used to underwrite for 100% of the loans.
items.selector_reason: 一笔住房净值交易首次使用VantageScore 4.0为全部贷款进行S&P初步评级，推动替代信用评分进入RMBS流程。该变化可能扩大借款人覆盖面并影响未来证券化标准。
items.title_zh: VantageScore获验证，可用于100%贷款RMBS评级
items.summary_zh: 首笔交易通过S&P Global初步评级流程，全部贷款采用VantageScore 4.0承保
